uncited: This family of methods addresses the fundamental limitation of vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the production of "floating" volumetric ellipsoids that lack an explicit, watertight geometric boundary .

By aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with continuous geometric priors (such as SDFs, depth maps, or explicit meshes), these methods enforce positional and normal consistency to enable accurate mesh extraction, physically-based rendering, and robust initialization .
See [Geometry and Surface Priors](9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md) for the shared mechanism, terms, and math .
Early works like [SuGaR](9191-sugar.md) introduced post-hoc regularization to flatten Gaussians into surfels.

Subsequent methods like [Geo-Splatting](9201-geo-splatting.md) integrated explicit meshes for physically-based rendering, while others like [GeoCE Loss](17334-geoce-loss.md) focused on feature-space geometric consistency.
